A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same Slow4Fast-VLN work, with directly matchable methods, results, and figures. v1 includes Appendix A.1–A.9; v2 ends with references and does not include its referenced supplementary material. The omissions assessed below concern the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSA-R2R navigation results, component and capacity ablations, trajectory case studies, and additional comparisons in Appendix Tables 6–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original navigation results in Tables 1–3, ablations in Tables 4–5, and qualitative trajectory studies.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the DUET policy, Llama3.2-vision reflection, structured experience retrieval, attention-based fusion, and instruction-style conversion. No procedural revision is stated. Omission of appendix pseudocode and implementation specifications does not establish that the underlying algorithm changed.

E1.justification: The principal GSA-R2R residential/non-residential coverage and Basic, Scene, and User instructions remain unchanged. v2 omits Appendix A.4's additional scenarios involving temporary obstacles, multiple obstructions, and visually confusable targets. Datasets listed only in v1's borrowed comparison table were not additional evaluations of this work.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. However, v2 omits the threshold-switching fast/slow baseline from Appendix A.4 and the MapGPT, NavCoT, and NavGPT-2 comparisons from Appendix A.6/Table 7, removing two substantive categories of comparative evidence.

E3.justification: v2 no longer reports Appendix A.4's separate evaluation design: 60 tasks across three environments, 20 tasks per difficulty level, switching thresholds of navigation error above 0.8 m and stagnation above 2 seconds, and time/FLOPs measurements. The shared benchmark settings and navigation metrics remain unchanged; this is an omitted protocol, not evidence of rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: The component ablations, experience-capacity sensitivity study, and both trajectory comparisons survive. Appendix A.5's visualization is relocated rather than newly added. The substantial removal is A.4's difficulty-stratified analysis testing whether experience reuse improves the efficiency–accuracy balance and robustness relative to threshold switching.

E5.justification: Tables 1–5 retain identical uncertainty entries and the same reporting practice. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval construction, or significance tests. Removing Table 6 removes results but does not change the uncertainty-reporting practice used in the retained experiments.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the retained case-study outcomes are unchanged. v2 removes Appendix Tables 6–7, including the hard-task comparison of 20.3 versus 12.1 seconds and 56.8 versus 13.2 GFLOPs for the threshold baseline versus Ours, and the separate LLM-method results. These are removed result sets, not same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 remain substantively unchanged, but v2 omits Appendix A.3's formal definitions of experience similarity, incremental updating, quality scoring, and cleanup in Equations 10–13. This removes the mathematical specification of experience-library management. Neither version presents theorem proofs.

C1.justification: v2 removes the introduction's explicit claim to be the first to incorporate instruction-language-style adaptability into GSA-VLN. The central claims about interactive fast/slow reasoning, experience reuse, instruction conversion, and navigation generalization remain.

C2.justification: v2 omits Appendix A.8's stated limitation that knowledge encoded through retraining is difficult to interpret, together with its proposed explicit knowledge-base direction. Interpretations attached to the omitted efficiency and LLM comparisons also disappear, while the main explanations of experience reuse, instruction conversion, and capacity effects remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 omits Algorithm 1, the complete reflection and instruction-conversion prompts in Figures 5–7, and library-management settings such as the 0.7 update threshold, 0.6 update weight, and 0.3 quality threshold. References to supplementary material do not supply these details within v2. The shared architecture details remain unchanged, so this is a substantial loss of reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The dedicated related-work discussion in Appendix A.1 and positioning against direct LLM navigation methods in A.6 disappear, substantially reducing coverage of VLN adaptation and fast/slow approaches. v2 adds citations including FSR-VLN and Vision-Language Navigation with Continual Learning, plus detection and driving works in the introduction. These are substantive citation and positioning changes beyond reference renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 removes the appendix organization, including standalone related-work and limitations sections, and integrates the former A.5 trajectory discussion into Section 3.2.1. It also removes the contribution-summary paragraph, shortens the conclusion, adds an acknowledgment, and redirects several cross-references to supplementary material. The structural revision is substantial despite largely unchanged retained prose.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with extensive resizing and reflow of tables and figures. v1 Figure 4 moves from the appendix to become v2 Figure 3, while the original Figure 3 becomes Figure 4. Algorithm 1, Tables 6–8, and Figures 5–8 are absent from v2; the retained trajectory graphics are not new analyses.

improvement.justification: Within the supplied PDFs, v2 substantially weakens reproducibility by omitting the full prompts, training pseudocode, and library-management specifications. It also removes the quantitative efficiency comparison and additional LLM comparisons while retaining the main framework claims and unchanged benchmark results. Bringing existing trajectory examples into the main text and moderating the priority claim provide limited benefits, but do not offset these losses of technical transparency and empirical support. The referenced supplementary material is not included in v2.
